sn22.7:1.2: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you how grasping leads to agitation, and how not grasping leads to freedom from agitation.
sn22.7:1.3: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”
sn22.7:2.1: “And how does grasping lead to agitation?
sn22.7:2.2: It’s when an unlearned ordinary person has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the true persons.
sn22.7:2.3: They regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.
sn22.7:2.4: But that form of theirs changes and is unstable,
sn22.7:2.5: and consciousness latches on to the change and alteration of form.
sn22.7:2.6: With the agitation born from the alteration in accordance with the change in form and coming from the co-arising of (unskillful mental) qualities, his mind stays consumed.
sn22.7:2.7: So they become frightened, worried, concerned, and agitated because of grasping.
sn22.7:5.1: They regard consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.
sn22.7:5.2: But that consciousness of theirs changes and is unstable,
sn22.7:5.3: and consciousness latches on to the change and alteration of consciousness.
sn22.7:5.4: With the agitation born from the alteration in accordance with the change in form and coming from the co-arising of (unskillful mental) qualities, his mind stays consumed.
sn22.7:5.5: So they become frightened, worried, concerned, and agitated because of grasping.
sn22.7:5.6: That’s how grasping leads to agitation.
sn22.7:6.1: And how does not grasping lead to freedom from agitation?
sn22.7:6.2: It’s when a learned noble disciple has seen the noble ones, and is skilled and trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve seen true persons, and are skilled and trained in the teaching of the true persons.
sn22.7:6.3: They don’t regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.
sn22.7:6.4: When that form of theirs changes and is unstable,
sn22.7:6.5: consciousness doesn’t latch on to the change and alteration of form.
sn22.7:6.6: Agitation—born of latching on to the change and alteration of form and originating in accordance with natural principles—don’t occupy their mind.
sn22.7:6.7: So they don’t become frightened, worried, concerned, or agitated because of grasping.
sn22.7:7.1: They don’t regard feeling as self …
sn22.7:8.1: They don’t regard perception as self …
sn22.7:8.2: They don’t regard choices as self …
sn22.7:9.1: They don’t regard consciousness as self …
sn22.7:9.2: When that consciousness of theirs changes and is unstable,
sn22.7:9.3: consciousness doesn’t latch on to the change and alteration of consciousness.
sn22.7:9.4: Agitation—born of latching on to the change and alteration of consciousness and originating in accordance with natural principles—don’t occupy their mind.
sn22.7:9.5: So they don’t become frightened, worried, concerned, or agitated because of grasping.
sn22.7:9.6: That’s how not grasping leads to freedom from agitation.”
